In this video, Dr. Paul Bilokon introduces reinforcement learning (RL), from its origins in the Industrial and Digital Revolutions to modern AI. He covers RL fundamentals—agents, actions, rewards—and its multidisciplinary scope across Engineering, Neuroscience, and Economics, distinguishing it from supervised and unsupervised learning. Case studies in games like Checkers and Go are mentioned by key concepts such as policies, value functions, and trial-and-error learning that drive reinforcement learning. He also discusses financial applications, with recommended papers and books, and answers questions on RL’s challenges in trading and integration with supervised learning features. This video offers insights for both beginners and professionals.

About the Speaker
Dr. Paul Bilokon, CEO and Founder of Thalesians Ltd, is a prominent figure in quantitative finance, algorithmic trading, and machine learning. He leads innovation in financial technology through his role at Thalesians Ltd and serves as Chief Scientific Advisor at Thalesians Marine Ltd. In addition to his industry work, he heads the faculty at the Machine Learning Institute and the Quantitative Developer Certificate, playing a key role in shaping the future of quantitative finance education.

[0:00] - Welcome and introduction to reinforcement learning
Dr. Paul Bilokon welcomes everyone and introduces what will be covered in the video.

[1:29] - Automation, the digital revolution, and intelligent machines
The Industrial Revolution boosted productivity with machines, while the Digital Revolution brought digital computers, paving the way for today’s information age.

[7:30] - Key components of reinforcement learning (agent, actions, rewards)
Alan Turing mentioned pain and pleasure stimuli to help cancel and invoke a response which are the key components of reinforcement learning today. 

[9:10] - Reinforcement learning is multidisciplinary
Includes several disciplines such as Engineering, Computer science, Neuroscience, Psychology, Economics and Mathematics. 

[10:38] - Reinforcement learning is neither supervised learning nor unsupervised learning
Relies on evaluated feedback to maximize returns, unlike supervised learning which uses exact solutions, as well as unsupervised learning that focuses on finding hidden structures.

[12:46] - Key components of reinforcement learning (agent, actions, rewards)
Agent takes actions according to the environment after taking in the observations in a state that agent perceives. Reward measures the success or failure of action which becomes a goal for the RL problem. 

[18:17] - Policies, value functions, model and trial & error in reinforcement learning with examples
Policy portrays the agent’s behavior, value function predicts rewards, and the model forecasts the environment’s response. Learning is shaped by trial and error, as seen in games like Checkers and Go.

[37:22] - Papers and books on financial applications of reinforcement learning
Interesting and useful papers as well as books are discussed and shared by Dr. Paul Bilokon that cater to the need of learning financial applications of RL.

[41:25] - Q&A: Challenges of RL in noisy financial environments
Typically ML is used to detect patterns and it works well when the signal-to-noise ratio is not so low. In trading, this is usually not the case. Can reinforcement learning be useful in trading?
